items.label: Industry: Quantum Computing Hardware & Infrastructure
items.detail: Selected via a live-searched news-prevalent theme: the IBKR connector was unauthenticated this session (non-interactive scheduled run, no OAuth flow available), so current holdings could not be pulled; the most recently confirmed holdings list (Oct 18 cycle: CCJ, CRWV, DBC, FCX, GOOG, IGLN, KGC, LLY, MPC, NEM, REMX, SSLV, TLT, TTWO, ULTA) has no quantum-computing exposure in any case, so this run went with the clearest unscouted news-prevalent theme instead. 2026 has been quantum computing's first real public-market test: Honeywell-backed Quantinuum's upsized $1.68B Nasdaq IPO (ticker QNT) priced at $60 and valued the company near $15.6B-$17.6B depending on source and timing; the US Department of Commerce signed letters of intent for equity stakes in nine quantum/advanced-tech firms (reportedly $1B to IBM, $375M to GlobalFoundries, $100M each to Quantinuum, Rigetti, Atom Computing, and Infleqtion); NVIDIA's NVQLink architecture (unveiled October 2025, extended with CUDA-Q Logical in 2026) now wires GPUs directly to 17 different QPU builders including IonQ, Rigetti, and Quantinuum; and Google's Willow-class error-correction results plus IBM's new 120-qubit Nighthawk chip and 2029 Starling fault-tolerance target keep the technology-milestone drumbeat constant. Not covered by any prior scout cycle (critical minerals/precious metals 2026-08-31, GLP-1 2026-08-31, gaming 2026-09-06, search/ads/cloud 2026-09-13, nuclear/SMR 2026-09-20, neoclouds 2026-09-27, beauty & personal care retail 2026-10-04, US oil refining 2026-10-11, humanoid robotics & industrial automation 2026-10-18).

items.label: QNT
items.detail: Quantinuum -- not held. The most complete full-stack pure play (trapped-ion hardware plus its own software/TKET stack), majority-backed by Honeywell (~48% voting power retained post-IPO), and a $100M recipient in the Commerce Department's quantum equity-stake program. Its upsized June 2026 IPO raised ~$1.68B at $60/share, above the marketed $53-55 range, and the stock opened near $68 before settling into a wide $51-68 range since -- valuation estimates range from ~$15.6B at pricing to ~$17.6B at the open, so treat any single figure as approximate. Real risk: revenue is tiny and lumpy (the March 2026 quarter reported just $5.2M, down from $19.1M a year earlier, with net loss widening to $136.6M) and has historically been concentrated in a handful of customers (Japan's RIKEN institute was ~90% of one recent quarter's revenue) -- this is a story stock priced on government and strategic backing plus a technology roadmap, not current financials. No live price available this session (IBKR connector unauthenticated); most recent open-web snapshot ~$53 (2026-08-26, from a secondary source, not independently verified).
items.diversification_note: No overlap with any current account holding (last confirmed list: CCJ, CRWV, DBC, FCX, GOOG, IGLN, KGC, LLY, MPC, NEM, REMX, SSLV, TLT, TTWO, ULTA); standalone new thematic exposure with no correlation to the account's current mining/energy/mega-cap-tech concentration.
items.suggested_size: Small speculative starter only -- this is the newest, most volatile, and most richly valued name in the group; size for binary technology-roadmap and revenue-concentration risk, not as a core position.

items.label: IONQ
items.detail: IonQ -- not held. The most commercially advanced trapped-ion pure play with a real, reported revenue base: Q2 2026 saw 60% of revenue from commercial (non-government) customers, though adjusted EBITDA was still -$120M. Deeply embedded in NVIDIA's NVQLink ecosystem as a launch hardware partner, with its next-generation Superion 256 system slated for first customer deliveries in 2027 and installation at NVIDIA's own quantum-AI computing center. Real risk: cash burn is large and the stock trades on sentiment as much as fundamentals -- open-web snapshots show a 52-week range of roughly $25.89-$84.64, with a mid-2026 reading near $34, so entry timing matters more here than for a typical new idea. No live price available this session (IBKR connector unauthenticated).
items.diversification_note: No overlap with any current holding; adds direct quantum-hardware exposure the account does not have, as a higher-revenue, higher-burn complement to QNT's full-stack bet.
items.suggested_size: Starter position; treat as the most commercially proven of the pure-play hardware names, but size modestly given the still-large EBITDA loss.

items.label: IBM
items.detail: IBM -- not held. The largest single recipient in the Commerce Department's quantum equity-stake program (a reported $1B letter of intent, roughly 2.7x Quantinuum's and 10x Rigetti's), and the superconducting-qubit leader with the sector's most concrete fault-tolerance roadmap: the 120-qubit Nighthawk chip is live today, the company is targeting a community-verified 'quantum advantage' milestone in 2026, and a fault-tolerant Starling system is roadmapped for 2029. This is the lowest-volatility way into the theme -- quantum sits inside a large, diversified, profitable technology business rather than being the whole investment case. Real risk: that diversification cuts both ways -- quantum revenue is immaterial to IBM's total results today, so near-term stock moves are driven by its much larger software/consulting/mainframe businesses, not quantum milestones; open-web snapshots also disagree sharply on price (~$299 in January 2026 vs. ~$237 in August 2026), so a meaningful move either way is plausible and needs a live quote to confirm. No live price available this session (IBKR connector unauthenticated).
items.diversification_note: No overlap with any current holding; adds large-cap diversified-technology exposure (software/consulting/mainframe plus a quantum call option) the account does not currently have in any form.
items.suggested_size: Starter position; treat as core large-cap technology exposure with a fault-tolerant-quantum call option attached, not as the primary way to express the quantum thesis.

items.label: HON
items.detail: Honeywell Technologies (ticker HON; renamed from Honeywell International after completing the June 29 2026 spin-off of Honeywell Aerospace Inc) -- not held. Retains roughly 48% of Quantinuum's voting power post-IPO, giving indirect exposure to the sector's largest pure play without the pure-play volatility. Not yet a specific call: the Quantinuum IPO triggered a one-time $6.6B GAAP deconsolidation gain that lifted Q2 2026 diluted EPS to $17.83, but adjusted EPS (which excludes that gain) actually fell 4% YoY to $4.52 -- so the headline number is an accounting event, not recurring quantum earnings, and the newly restructured entity (post-Aerospace spin-off) needs at least one more clean reporting quarter before its underlying trend is readable.

items.label: RGTI
items.detail: Rigetti Computing -- not held. A $100M Commerce Department letter of intent and an NVQLink hardware partner, with Q2 2026 revenue of $5.1M (up from $1.8M a year earlier) showing real if small growth -- but the quarter still missed consensus EPS estimates, and the stock has been extraordinarily volatile on sentiment rather than fundamentals, with open-web snapshots ranging from roughly $12 (mid-2025) to a brief spike above $35 (late 2025) back down to the mid-teens by mid-2026. Worth tracking as the pure-play superconducting name once revenue scales past its current single-digit-million run rate, not a call today.

items.label: Quantum computing forecasting uncertainty and the post-quantum cryptography deadline
items.detail: No specific ticker -- two risks sitting under every name in this report. First, market-size estimates for 2026 alone range from roughly $1.8B to $8.6B depending on the research provider, with projected 2030-2036 endpoints spanning an even wider $7.3B-$198B -- a sector-defining disagreement that makes any single TAM figure in this report a placeholder, not a forecast. Second, NIST's draft timeline would begin deprecating RSA/ECDSA by 2030 and disallow them by 2035 on 'harvest now, decrypt later' grounds, a genuine multi-year regulatory tailwind for the cryptography-migration side of this theme (not covered by the hardware names above) but also a reminder that the hardware names' near-term economics still depend on government and strategic funding rather than this migration demand, which remains several years out. Separately, early evidence suggests US export controls on Chinese quantum firms (QuantumCTek entity-listed, cryogenics/control-electronics licensing requirements) may be accelerating rather than slowing Chinese domestic capability (China reportedly went from zero to 10+ domestic dilution-refrigerator makers by 2026) -- the same policy-reversibility risk flagged in prior cycles for other tariff-dependent theses, worth revisiting each cycle rather than treating as settled.
